title: Neural signaling contributes to heart formation and growth in the invertebrate chordate, Ciona robusta
experiments_summary: The study employed a broad range of experimental approaches to investigate heart anatomy, growth, and neural regulation in Ciona robusta. (1) Whole-mount confocal microscopy with DAPI, phalloidin, and WGA staining was used to generate high-resolution microanatomical maps of adult and juvenile hearts, distinguishing myocardium, pericardium, epicardium, and undifferentiated line (UL) cell types. (2) EdU pulse and pulse-chase experiments with varying durations (30 min to 24 hours) were conducted in adult and juvenile hearts to quantify proliferation rates in distal versus midline UL regions and to assess proliferative indices of distinct progenitor populations. (3) Clonal analysis using short 30-min EdU pulses followed by 72-hour chases was performed to characterize division patterns of UL cells. (4) Lineage tracing used a photoconvertible Kaede fluorescent reporter driven by the Mesp regulatory element (Mesp>Kaede::NLS) in stable transgenic lines; individual UL cells or clusters were photoconverted and imaged every 24 hours for up to five days to track symmetric and asymmetric divisions and precursor migration. (5) Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was performed on dissociated adult heart cells from two biological replicates using a 10x Genomics-based encapsulation protocol optimized for marine organisms; bioinformatic analysis used Scanpy with PCA, UMAP, and Louvain clustering, and blood cell clusters were identified by Pearson correlation with a published C. robusta blood cell scRNA-seq dataset. Sub-cluster analyses were performed on the UL (Cluster 7) and neural-like (Cluster 8) clusters separately. (6) Fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH) was used to validate spatial expression patterns of marker genes including CrUL1, Gata.a, and TACR in juvenile hearts. (7) Reporter transgenic lines (PC2>Kaede, VACHT>CFP, TH>Kaede, Syt15>GFP, TK>CFP, Mesp>RFP) were deployed in stable transgenic animals to localize distinct neural-like and cardiac cell populations in adult and juvenile hearts at multiple developmental stages. (8) Heart rate quantification was performed on D5-D6 juveniles before and after pharmacological treatment with AMPT, acetylcholine chloride, and the TACR inhibitor Aprepitant; paired t-tests were used for statistical analysis. (9) Pharmacological gain- and loss-of-function assays tested the role of canonical Wnt (cWnt) signaling using IWR-1-endo (cWnt inhibitor), BIO (GSK3 inhibitor), and SKL2001 (Axin/β-catenin disruptor), followed by EdU pulse assays in juvenile hearts. (10) A dominant-negative TCF transgene (Foxf∆epi>TCFdn) was electroporated into embryos to disrupt cWnt signaling specifically in cardiac lineage cells; resulting juvenile hearts were compared to Foxf∆epi>LacZ controls for UL cell number and heart morphology. (11) Pharmacological inhibition of tachykinin signaling used two distinct TACR antagonists—Aprepitant and Spantide II—applied to D3 juveniles for four days, followed by EdU labeling and UL cell counting in D7 animals. Controls included Atropine (cholinergic antagonist), Doxazosin Mesylate (alpha-1 adrenergic antagonist), and AMPT (TH inhibitor). (12) A gain-of-function tachykinin experiment used Ramipril (ACE inhibitor that blocks tachykinin degradation) to assess effects on midline progenitor numbers. (13) Direct injection of Aprepitant or Atropine into adult C. robusta hearts was performed via microinjection through a tunic incision, followed by 24-hour culture and EdU labeling of excised hearts; EdU+ and DAPI+ nuclei were quantified using CellProfiler. (14) CRISPR-Cas9 knockdown experiments targeted tachykinin (TK) using PC2>Cas9 with two TK-specific sgRNAs (TKsgRNA2, TKsgRNA3), and targeted TACR using Mesp>Cas9 with two TACR-specific sgRNAs (TACRsgRNA2, TACRsgRNA3), all co-electroporated with PC2>Kaede to visualize cardiac neural plexuses; juvenile hearts were analyzed at D10 for morphology, presence of myocardium, PC2+ plexuses, and CrUL1 expression. Targeting efficiency was validated by Sanger sequencing of PCR-amplified genomic regions from pooled transgenic larvae. (15) High-intensity confocal imaging was used to visualize potential extrinsic innervation by following PC2>Kaede-labeled projections from the central ganglia to cardiac neural plexuses in adult and D10 juvenile animals. Statistical analyses included t-tests, paired t-tests, Fisher's exact test, and permutation tests as appropriate for each experimental comparison.
